Description: implicit — nothing above the horizon once the camera is pitched
prompt: My MapLibre GL JS map has 3D terrain enabled and the camera pitched to 70 degrees. The relief looks right, but everything above the horizon line is the flat page background. I want an actual sky and some haze where the ground meets it. How do I set that up?
[groq-gpt-oss] evals/prompts/lib/skill-p:
Below is a **complete, copy-and-paste ready** recipe that turns the blank “page-background” you see above the horizon into a real sky with a gentle haze (fog) that blends into the terrain. All of the pieces are part of the **core MapLibre GL JS API** – there is no “sky layer” to add, the sky lives at the **root level** of the style (or can be set later with `map.setSky()`). --- ## 1️⃣ Prerequisites – you already have these ```js // 1️⃣ Create the map const map = new maplibregl.Map({ container: 'map', // id of the
style: 'https://demotiles.maplibre.org/style.json', // any style you like center: [13.4, 52.5], // lon, lat zoom: 12, pitch: 70, // you already set this bearing: 0, antialias: true // recommended for terrain + sky }); // 2️⃣ Add a raster-DEM source (the same one you already use for terrain) map.addSource('terrain-dem', { type: 'raster-dem', url: 'https://tiles.mapterhorn.com/tilejson.json', // ← your DEM source tileSize: 256, maxzoom: 12 }); // 3️⃣ Turn the DEM into 3-D terrain map.setTerrain({ source: 'terrain-dem', exaggeration: 1 }); ``` If you can already see the hills and valleys, the three lines above are already in your code. Now we only need to **add the sky**. --- ## 2️⃣ Add a sky object (the “blank horizon” disappears) ### Option A – **Declarative** (put it directly into the style JSON) If you control the style JSON (e.g. you load a local file or generate it on the fly), add a top-level `sky` object: ```json { "version": 8, "sources": { … }, "layers": [ … ], "sky": { "sky-type": "atmosphere", // only “atmosphere” is supported "sky-color": "#199EF3", // bright-blue daytime sky "sky-horizon-blend": 0.5, // how quickly the sky fades to the horizon "horizon-color": "#ffffff", // near-white at the horizon line "horizon-fog-blend": 0.5, // blend horizon → fog "fog-color": "#cce6ff", // light blue-gray haze "fog-ground-blend": 0.3, // how far the fog reaches down onto the terrain "atmosphere-blend": 0.25 // optional extra atmospheric glow } } ``` > **Note:** The `sky` object lives **outside** the `layers` array – it is a sibling of `sources`, `layers`, `glyphs`, etc. ### Option B – **Imperative** (add it after the map has been created) If you load a remote style that you cannot edit, you can inject the sky at runtime: ```js map.on('load', () => { // 1️⃣ Make sure terrain is already on (you already called setTerrain) // 2️⃣ Add the sky map.setSky({ 'sky-type': 'atmosphere', // only value supported by MapLibre 'sky-color': '#199EF3', 'sky-horizon-blend': 0.5, 'horizon-color': '#ffffff', 'horizon-fog-blend': 0.5, 'fog-color': '#cce6ff', 'fog-ground-blend': 0.3, 'atmosphere-blend': 0.25 }); }); ``` Both approaches produce the same visual result – pick the one that fits your workflow. --- ## 3️⃣ Why the sky only appears when **terrain** is on * The sky (and the fog that blends into it) are **tied to the 3-D terrain mesh**. * If `map.setTerrain(null)` is called, the sky is automatically hidden and you’ll see the plain background again. * The sky also needs a **non-zero pitch** – you already have `pitch: 70`, so you’re good. --- ## 4️⃣ Tweaking the look | Property | What it does | Typical range | |----------|--------------|---------------| | `sky-color` | Base colour of the dome (high in the sky) | `#87CEEB` (light blue) → `#001848` (deep twilight) | | `sky-horizon-blend` | How quickly the colour fades toward the horizon | `0.0` (no fade) → `1.0` (instant) | | `horizon-color` | Colour exactly at the horizon line | Usually a very light version of `sky-color` or white | | `horizon-fog-blend` | How much the horizon colour mixes into the fog | `0.0` → `1.0` | | `fog-color` | Colour of the haze that sits on the terrain | Light blues, greys, or even a sunset pink | | `fog-ground-blend` | How far the fog reaches down the terrain (0 = only at the horizon, 1 = covers the whole ground) | `0.2`–`0.5` works well for a subtle haze | | `atmosphere-blend` | Extra “glow” around the sun direction (only visible when `sky-type: "atmosphere"`). | `0.0`–`0.5` | Play with the numbers in the live example below until you get the exact mood you want. --- ## 5️⃣ Full working example (HTML + JS) ```html MapLibre – Terrain + Sky + Fog
``` Open the file in a browser (or paste it into a CodePen/JSFiddle) and you’ll see: * The terrain you already had. * A blue-sky dome that follows the camera’s rotation. * A soft, light-blue haze that meets the ground at the horizon. --- ## 6️⃣ Common pitfalls & how to avoid them | Symptom | Cause | Fix | |---------|-------|-----| | **Sky stays black / background shows** | `map.setTerrain(null)` or terrain source not loaded yet. | Call `setTerrain` **before** `setSky`, or wait for the `load` event as in the example. | | **Fog never appears** | `fog-color` is the same as `sky-color` or `fog-ground-blend` is `0`. | Use a slightly different colour (e.g. a lighter blue) and set `fog-ground-blend` ≥ 0.2. | | **Sky looks flat, no horizon blend** | `sky-horizon-blend` set to `0`. | Increase to `0.4–0.6`. | | **Sky disappears after style change** | Loading a new style overwrites the root-level `sky` object. | Re-apply `map.setSky()` after each `map.setStyle()` (listen to the `styledata` event). | | **Performance drops on low-end devices** | Very high `exaggeration` + high `pitch` + many draped raster layers. | Keep `exaggeration` modest (≤ 2), limit raster overlays, and enable `antialias: true` only if you need smooth edges. | --- ## 7️⃣ Quick checklist (copy-paste into your notes) ```text [ ] DEM source added (type: raster-dem) [ ] map.setTerrain({source: 'your-dem', exaggeration: 1}) [ ] map.setSky({ 'sky-type': 'atmosphere', 'sky-color': '#199EF3', 'sky-horizon-blend': 0.5, 'horizon-color': '#ffffff', 'horizon-fog-blend': 0.5, 'fog-color': '#cce6ff', 'fog-ground-blend': 0.3, 'atmosphere-blend': 0.25 }) [ ] map pitch > 0 (you have 70°) [ ] Verify fog-ground-blend ≠ 0 and fog-color ≠ sky-color [ ] If you swap styles, re-run map.setSky() ``` --- ### TL;DR 1. **Enable terrain** (`map.setTerrain` – you already did this). 2. **Add a sky object** (either in the style JSON under the top-level key `sky`, or at runtime with `map.setSky`). 3. Choose colours and blend values that give you the desired blue-sky + haze effect. 4. Keep the camera pitched (you have 70°) and the sky will replace the blank page background. That’s it – you now have a proper sky with atmospheric fog that blends into your 3-D terrain. Happy mapping!
